vulnerability_analysis: The approve function in BNRG contract doesn't follow the ERC20 standard pattern of requiring allowance to be set to 0 before changing it. This creates a race condition where a spender can front-run an approve transaction to steal tokens. When a victim tries to change an existing approval from amount X to amount Y, the spender can front-run the approval change with a transferFrom to use amount X, and then still have allowance Y after the approval change goes through.
attack_strategy: Simulate the approve race condition by: 1) Setting up a victim with tokens, 2) Having victim approve attacker for amount X, 3) Having victim try to change approval to amount Y, 4) Front-running the approval change to use amount X, 5) Then using the new allowance Y.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Create a victim address and give it tokens. 2. Have victim approve attacker for 1000 tokens. 3. Have victim try to change approval to 500 tokens. 4. Front-run the approval change by calling transferFrom to take 1000 tokens. 5. After approval change, call transferFrom again to take 500 tokens. 6. Total stolen: 1500 tokens.
